title: Maximal boundedness of integral points of a split reductive model
statement: Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] with algebraically closed residue field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], fraction field $L$ and normalized valuation $v:L^\times\to\mathbf Z$, extended by $v(0)=+\infty$. Let $\mathcal D$ be a split reductive $R$-group scheme: a smooth affine finite-type group scheme with reductive geometric fibres and a closed subgroup $\mathcal T\cong\mathbf G_{m,R}^{r}$ maximal among tori in each geometric fibre. Group schemes over a ring have multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with that ring as base. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme].Over a field, reductive means smooth, geometrically connected, affine of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after algebraic closure; unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Here $\mathbf G_{m,R}=\operatorname{Spec}R[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units, and a torus over an algebraically closed field is a finite product of $\mathbf G_m$. Put $G=\mathcal D_L$. For an $R$-algebra $S$, write $\mathcal D(S)$ for morphisms of $R$-schemes $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\mathcal D$, with the group structure induced by multiplication. Regard $\mathcal D(R)$ as a subgroup of $G(L)$ by generic restriction. Call a subgroup $M\subseteq G(L)$ bounded if for every regular function $f\in L[G]$ there exists $n_f\in\mathbf Z$ such that $v(f(x))\geq n_f$ for all $x\in M$. Then $\mathcal D(R)$ is bounded, and every bounded subgroup $M$ of $G(L)$ containing $\mathcal D(R)$ equals $\mathcal D(R)$. No completeness or local compactness of $L$ is assumed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0405381: Lemma 3.7 (first assertion, the Iwahori--Matsumoto maximal-boundedness statement) and its application in Proposition 4.3, second paragraph, printed pp.7-8

proof.text: Write $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The affine-spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies $R$-points with $R$-algebra maps $A\to R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] $G=\mathcal D\times_R\operatorname{Spec}L$ is affine with $L[G]=A\otimes_R L$, and $A\otimes_RL=S^{-1}A$, where $S=R\setminus\{0\}$, since $L=S^{-1}R$ and a ring map out of either side is exactly a ring map out of $A$ inverting the image of $S$. Thus each $f\in L[G]$ is $a/s$ with $a\in A$, $0\ne s\in R$. For every integral point $x$, $a(x)\in R$, so $v(f(x))\geq-v(s)$. This includes $a(x)=0$ under the stated convention for $v(0)$, and proves boundedness of $K:=\mathcal D(R)$. Its generic restriction is injective: if two maps $A\to R$ agree in $L$, they agree in the subring $R\subset L$. The valuation-ring description of a DVR is [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring].

source.place: Lemma 3.7, first assertion: agent coordinate-ring proof of boundedness, using affine definitions.

proof.text: Let $M\subseteq G(L)$ be a bounded subgroup containing $K$, and fix $m\in M$. Apply [lem-sfb-split-reductive-dvr-cartan-decomposition] to the given split reductive model and its given closed split maximal torus. All its hypotheses are in the statement of the item; henselianity and algebraic closedness of the residue field are more than the decomposition needs. Obtain $m=k_1tk_2$, where $k_1,k_2\in K$ and $t\in T(L)$. Since $K\subseteq M$ and $M$ is a subgroup, $t=k_1^{-1}mk_2^{-1}\in M$, and $t^n\in M$ for every integer $n\geq1$.

source.place: WANTED locally; author-hosted PDF https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf, Theorem 4.1 and Remark 4.2, printed p.7, together with the fixed-torus formulation in Remark 3.5, printed p.5.

proof.text: Use the chosen splitting $\mathcal T\cong\mathbf G_{m,R}^r$ and write $t=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in(L^\times)^r$. By the affine description of a closed immersion in [def-weil-closed-immersion], the restriction $A\to R[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ is surjective. Choose lifts $b_j,c_j\in A$ of $z_j,z_j^{-1}$. Their images in $L[G]$ are regular functions, so boundedness of $M$ supplies integers $B_j,C_j$ such that for every $n\geq1$, $B_j\leq v(b_j(t^n))=n v(a_j)$ and $C_j\leq v(c_j(t^n))=-n v(a_j)$. If $v(a_j)>0$ the second right-hand side tends to minus infinity, contradicting $C_j$; if $v(a_j)<0$ the first contradicts $B_j$. Hence $v(a_j)=0$ for each $j$. No extension of a character as a group homomorphism on $G$ is asserted: only its lift as an element of the coordinate ring is used.

source.place: Tag 01QO, morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion (2), as stated by def-weil-closed-immersion; agent integer-valuation calculation.

proof.text: By the valuation-ring description of [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $v(a_j)=0$ implies $a_j,a_j^{-1}\in R$, hence $a_j\in R^\times$. Thus $t\in\mathcal T(R)\subseteq K$, and $m=k_1tk_2\in K$. As $m$ was arbitrary, $M\subseteq K$; the assumed reverse inclusion gives $M=K$. For $r=0$ there are no coordinates and $T(L)=\{1\}$, so the same argument applies with an empty list. Together with step 1 this proves both requested assertions without any completeness or compactness argument.
